findings.title: A hung flusher process is no longer killed before its replacement starts.
findings.body:
In production, flusher processes are created with `mp_context.Process` from the spawn context, so they are `SpawnProcess` objects. `SpawnProcess` subclasses `BaseProcess`, not `multiprocessing.Process`, so `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is always False and `kill()` is never called. The old code called `self.process.kill()` with no condition.

When a process is restarted for `hang`, the stuck process keeps running and a second one starts for the same shards. The two share the same `stopped`, `healthy_since` and `backpressure_since` values. If the old one recovers, both flush the same segments and produce duplicates. Each restart can leak another process, up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS of them.

Fix: call `kill()` on anything that is not a `threading.Thread`, for example `if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread): process.kill()`, or check against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`.

findings.title: The added `time.sleep(0.1)` does nothing because the test replaces `time.sleep` with a no-op.
findings.body:
`test_basic` calls `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`, so the new `time.sleep(0.1)` returns immediately. It gives the flusher thread no time to process after the drift change.

The test still races: `step.join()` sets `stopped`, and the thread can exit before it flushes the segment. When that happens `(msg,) = messages` fails, so the test stays flaky.

Fix: wait for the result explicitly, for example poll until `messages` is non-empty within a deadline before calling `join()`, or keep a reference to the real sleep before patching it.

findings.title: The `wait_produce` metric uses the tag key `shards`; the other new metrics use `shard`.
findings.body: `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` are tagged with `shard`, but `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` is tagged with `shards`. Dashboards or queries that filter on `shard` will miss this metric. Use the same key for all of them.
